source_text: Sed uniuersa nomina criminum discedant in operum suorum proprietates, remaneat idololatria in eo quod ipsa est. sufficit sibi tam inimicum deo nomen, tam locuples substantia criminis, quae tot ramos porrigit, tot uenas diffundit, ut de hoc cum maxime materia suscepta sit, quot modis nobis praecauenda sit idololatriae latitudo, quoniam multifariam seruos dei nec tantum ignorata, sed etiam dissimulata subuertit. plerique idololatrian simpliciter existimant his solis modis interpretandam, si quis aut incendat aut immolet aut polluceat aut sacris aliquibus aut sacerdotiis obligetur, quemadmodum si quis existimet adulterium in osculis et in amplexibus et in ipsa carnis congressione censendum aut homicidium in sola sanguinis profusione et in animae ereptione reputandum. at enim, dominus, quam eextensius ista disponat, certi sumus, cum adulterium etiam in concupiscentia designat, si oculum quis impegerit libidinose et animam commouerit impudice, cum homicidium etiam in uerbo maledicti uel conuicii iudicat et in omni impetu irae et in neglegentia caritatis in fratrem. sicut Iohannes docet homicidam esse qui oderit fratrem. alioquin in modico consisteret et diaboli ingenium de malitia et dei dominium de disciplina, qua nos aduersus diaboli latitudines munit, si in his tantum delictis iudicaremur, quae etiam nationes decreuerunt uindicanda. quomodo abundabit iustitia nostra super scribas et pharisaeos, ut dominus praescripsit, nisi abundantiam aduersariae eius id est iniustitiae perspexerimus? quod si caput iniustitiae idololatria est, prius est, uti aduersus abundantiam idololatriae praemuniamur, dum illam non solum in manifestis recognoscimus.
thought_title: Idolatry's breadth must be recognized, not narrowed
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that idolatry is the chief sin and must be understood in its full extent, not reduced to a few obvious acts.
pass_a_gloss: But let all the names of crimes depart into the properties of their own works; let idolatry remain in that which it itself is. A name so hostile to God is sufficient for itself, so rich a substance of crime, which extends so many branches, spreads so many veins, that from this especially material has been taken up, in how many ways the breadth of idolatry must be guarded against by us, since in many ways it subverts the servants of God, not only unknown but also disguised. Many people think idolatry is simply to be interpreted in these ways alone, if anyone either burns incense or sacrifices or offers a sacrificial meal or is bound to some sacred rites or priesthoods, just as if anyone should think adultery is to be judged in kisses and in embraces and in the very union of flesh, or homicide is to be reckoned in the shedding of blood alone and in the taking of life. But indeed, how much more extensively the Lord arranges these things, we are certain, when he marks adultery also in desire, if anyone has struck his eye lustfully and has stirred his soul shamelessly, when he judges homicide also in a word of cursing or insult and in every impulse of anger and in negligence of love toward a brother. Just as John teaches that he who hates his brother is a murderer. Otherwise the devil's cleverness about malice and God's lordship about discipline, by which he fortifies us against the devil's expanses, would consist in a small matter, if we were judged only in those offenses which even the nations have decreed must be punished. How will our righteousness abound above the scribes and Pharisees, as the Lord prescribed, unless we have perceived the abundance of its adversary, that is, of injustice? But if the head of injustice is idolatry, it is first that we be fortified in advance against the abundance of idolatry, while we recognize it not only in its open forms.

choices.why: Fixed glossary term; must use the glossary English.
Polluceo refers specifically to offering a sacred feast or sacrificial meal, distinct from immolo (sacrifice) and incendo (burn incense).
Plural abstract noun for priestly offices; keeps the sense of being bound to pagan religious offices.
Literal rendering of the physical sexual act, matching Tertullian's concrete list of acts.
Keeps the spatial metaphor of breadth that Tertullian uses for the devil's scope, parallel to 'breadth of idolatry'.
The verb means to fortify beforehand; preserves the military metaphor of defense against idolatry.

pass_b_english: But let all the names of crimes go off to the particular acts that belong to them, and let idolatry remain in what it itself is. A name so hostile to God is enough for it, and so rich a substance of crime, which stretches out so many branches and spreads so many veins, that from this especially material should be taken for how many ways the breadth of idolatry must be guarded against by us, since in many ways it overturns the servants of God, not only when it is unknown but even when it is ignored.

Most people think idolatry is to be understood only in these ways: if someone burns incense or sacrifices or offers a sacrificial meal or is bound to some sacred rites or priesthoods. That is like someone thinking adultery is to be counted only in kisses and embraces and in the actual union of flesh, or homicide only in the shedding of blood and the taking of a life.

But how much more widely the Lord arranges these things, we are certain, when he marks adultery even in desire, if someone fixes his eye lustfully and stirs his soul shamelessly (Matthew 5:28), when he judges homicide even in a word of cursing or insult and in every impulse of anger and in neglect of love for a brother (Matthew 5:22). So John teaches that whoever hates his brother is a murderer (1 John 3:15).

Otherwise the devil's cleverness in evil and God's lordship over discipline, by which he fortifies us against the expanses of the devil, would consist in very little, if we were judged only in those offenses which even the pagans have decreed must be punished. How will our righteousness abound beyond the scribes and Pharisees, as the Lord prescribed (Matthew 5:20), unless we have seen the abundance of its adversary, that is, of injustice? But if the head of injustice is idolatry, the first thing is that we be fortified in advance against the abundance of idolatry, while we recognize it not only in its open forms.

last_rejected.fix: translate as “defiles” or “pollutes” rather than “offers a sacrificial meal”.
last_rejected.ruling: polluceat from polleo/polluceo means 'offer a feast/sacrifice'; polluo 'defile' is a different verb. Translation is correct.

problems.why: Same concept (non-Christians) rendered as 'nations,' 'pagans,' and 'outsiders' interchangeably.
problems.fix: Use 'pagans' consistently or note that 'nations' = pagans.

fixed: Changed 'the nations' to 'the pagans' for ethnici/nationes per glossary: the source 'nationes' refers to non-Christian pagans, and the glossary requires 'pagans' for this concept.

problems.why: 'Genius' in modern sense of brilliance is misleading; Latin 'ingenium' means nature/cleverness.
problems.fix: Change to 'the devil's cleverness in evil'.

fixed: Changed 'genius for evil' to 'cleverness in evil' because Latin 'ingenium' here means nature or cleverness, not brilliance in the modern sense.

polish.changed: Clarified the flow of Tertullian's argument by breaking the dense opening into four paragraphs, making the contrast between common assumptions and the Lord's wider teaching easier to follow, and ensuring consistent use of 'pagans' for non-Christians.
